items.difficulty_reason: The theorem states that a simple finite algebra over a field is a matrix algebra over a finite skew field (statement lines 357-364). The proof is a complete argument: a simple submodule is chosen and its endomorphism ring is a skew field by a named lemma (proof lines 366-369); Rieffel's theorem identifies the algebra with the endomorphisms of that module over the skew field (proof lines 370-372); and finite dimensionality makes the module finite free over the skew field, so its endomorphism ring is a matrix algebra over the opposite skew field (proof lines 373-375). The non-formal content is the choice of the module and the freeness step. The claim is H2.
